title: Normalized scalar comparison on shifted root lines
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an algebra homomorphism $a:E\to L$, a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and $d\ge0$. Use the completed coefficient categories and rationalization of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the shifted root complex $C_{X,d}$ of [def-sf-orientation-integral-line-comparisons]. Regard $QC_{X,d}$ as the actual finite-Tor constructible completed line; the one-term shift comparison identifies it with $\mathcal O_E(d)[2d]$. Define its completed scalar comparison by the inverse scalar-completion augmentation, ordinary scalar extension on the complex, and the root-normalized ordinary scalar-line comparison. Its lift to the integral representative of rational scalar extension is uniquely characterized by that underlying morphism. The rational comparison is the image of this lift under the specified rational localization. In particular it is fixed on every local root tensor and includes identity and composite coefficient extensions. For spaces over the fixed field of [def-sf-datum], geometric invertibility supplies these comparisons without extra assumptions; their finite-field transition coordinates use the actual stage-system scalar comparison.
